summary: Ten household countries with a real curve: the US, China, France, Russia and Japan come fast, Canada and South Korea are the stretch. Weapons guesses and Germany burn lives quickly, so a casual player stops around 8.
reasons: A casual found 8 in 13 guesses (all but Canada and South Korea) and ran out of lives on Germany, Iran, North Korea, Israel and Pakistan. A fan found all 10 in 11 guesses, one life on Sweden (#12). Crowd average about 5.9, on target.

The prompt steers to power ("nuclear power reactors in use") but the title only says "nuclear reactors", and weapons guesses still cost lives. Iran (#28, 1) and Pakistan (#12, 6) teach something, and Germany's "none since its phase-out in 2023" is a good reveal. North Korea and Israel only say "outside the top 28", which sounds like a near miss for countries with no power reactors at all.

Figures match the source table and #10 UK (9) vs #11 Spain (7) is clean. Japan's 15 leave out 18 suspended reactors, but Ukraine's 15 include Zaporizhzhia's six, shut down since Russia seized it. That reorders #8 to #10 but changes no member. Distinct from oil-production and co2-emissions (France #3, Ukraine, South Korea).
fixes: Add notes for the famous countries with no power reactors that players will type: North Korea, Israel, Australia, Saudi Arabia get "none". Today each reads "North Korea is outside the top 28. Lost a life." with no figure.
Title: "Countries with the most nuclear power reactors" (46 characters). The h1 is read first, and the steer away from weapons only sits in the caption today.

Ukraine's fact: say its 15 include Zaporizhzhia's six, Europe's largest plant, shut down since Russian forces seized it in March 2022 (Nuclear power in Ukraine: "occupied and claimed by Russia and shutdown"). Japan's idle reactors don't count, and an informed player will ask.
Japan's fact says only 13 ran again by late 2024, next to a shown 15: use the source table's 15 in use and 18 suspended.
The topic renames Türkiye to Turkey, but the build still shows "Türkiye" (the universe's name, matched from the table's "Turkey"): the rename doesn't take.
